subsystems.name: Function-polynomial design
subsystems.role: converts the operation you want into a polynomial that can be applied to eigenvalues or singular values.
parts: approximation of the target function (e.g. 1/x, sign, exponential)
parity and degree constraints keeping the polynomial bounded by 1 on [-1,1]
error analysis trading accuracy against degree

subsystems.name: Block encoding
subsystems.role: embeds the matrix, Hamiltonian or data set inside a larger unitary that the circuit can apply.

subsystems.name: Phase-factor solver
subsystems.role: computes the angles classically from the target polynomial.

subsystems.name: Signal-processing circuit
subsystems.role: the actual sequence: one qubit rotated, interleaved with controlled applications of the encoded unitary.
parts: Z-rotations by twice each phase angle
final measurement of the signal qubit

subsystems.name: Compiler and resource estimator
subsystems.role: turns ideal rotations into a gate sequence a real machine can run.
parts: angle synthesis into a finite fault-tolerant gate set

subsystems.name: Readout and post-processing
subsystems.role: extracts a usable answer from the transformed state.

buildSteps.title: State the target as a spectral transformation
buildSteps.detail: Write the problem as a function to be applied to the eigenvalues of a unitary or the singular values of a matrix — for example inverting a matrix, simulating time evolution, or projecting onto a low-energy subspace.

buildSteps.title: Choose the approximating polynomial
buildSteps.detail: Find a bounded polynomial that matches the target function to the required precision, with the correct parity so it can be realised by the rotation sequence.

buildSteps.title: Solve for the phase sequence
buildSteps.detail: A classical program finds the angles such that the product of rotations and controlled unitary applications has the polynomial sitting in the top-left entry of the resulting matrix; this is a numerically delicate root-finding problem whose difficulty grows with polynomial degree.

buildSteps.title: Block-encode the input
buildSteps.detail: Build the circuit that embeds the Hamiltonian or matrix using linear combinations of unitaries or qubitisation techniques, accepting a subnormalisation factor that sets the overall scale.

buildSteps.title: Compose the signal-processing circuit
buildSteps.detail: Prepare the signal qubit, then interleave controlled applications of the encoded unitary with Z-rotations by twice each phase angle — the heart of the construction.

buildSteps.title: Compile for fault tolerance
buildSteps.detail: Synthesise every arbitrary rotation into a discrete error-corrected gate set, tracking how the compilation error adds to the approximation error.

buildSteps.title: Validate on small instances
buildSteps.detail: Simulate the compiled circuit classically on tiny problems where the answer is known, checking that the measured signal-qubit statistics reproduce the intended polynomial.

buildSteps.title: Run and post-process
buildSteps.detail: Execute many repetitions on hardware, then convert measurement frequencies into the transformed value — an energy, a solution vector or a matrix function.

prerequisites.why: useful applications need thousands of logical qubits and millions of gates, far beyond today's machines.
small codes have been run, but not long enough or large enough to sustain algorithm-length circuits.
linear-combination-of-unitaries and qubitisation constructions are well developed in theory and shown in small experiments.
the phase factors are computed on ordinary computers, though high-degree cases strain numerical precision.

prerequisites.tech: High-fidelity single-qubit control and rotation synthesis
prerequisites.why: the sequence is built from precise rotations, so each one must be accurate and reproducible.

pathway.milestone: the framework is fully worked out and unifies many separate quantum algorithms under one recipe
pathway.unlocks: a single design method for Hamiltonian simulation, matrix inversion, ground-state and optimisation problems.

pathway.milestone: small end-to-end runs on early error-corrected hardware for problems solvable classically
pathway.unlocks: confidence that compiled phase sequences behave as predicted outside simulation.

pathway.milestone: resource-optimised versions with drastically lower gate counts
pathway.unlocks: fitting practical chemistry and materials problems inside realistic hardware budgets.

pathway.milestone: fault-tolerant machines running these circuits at useful scale
pathway.unlocks: quantum advantage on problems where classical simulation is hopeless.
